bug_description.original: Crash Type: Global-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 Crash State: template_fuzzer.cc Crash Address: 0x0000011aa460
bug_description.normalized: In the template fuzzer harness LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput, the size-clamping guard uses a strict greater-than comparison (size > sizeof(copy)) instead of greater-than-or-equal. When the fuzzer input is exactly 32768 bytes (equal to sizeof(copy)), the comparison evaluates to false and size is not clamped to sizeof(copy)-1. The subsequent NUL-termination copy[size] = '\0' then writes 1 byte past the end of the 32768-byte global static array copy, causing a global-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1.

source.description: Attacker-controlled data and size are materialized into the 32768-byte global static array copy via memcpy. With the unclamped size=32768, the entire buffer is filled, and the same unclamped size value is subsequently used to index copy for NUL-termination.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled fuzzer input (data, size); size equals exactly sizeof(copy) = 32768, bypassing the off-by-one guard.

sink.description: With size=32768, copy[32768] writes the NUL terminator 1 byte past the end of the 32768-byte global array copy (valid indices 0..32767). ASAN detects global-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 at 0x0000011aa460, 0 bytes to the right of the global variable.

root_cause.description: The size-clamping guard uses strict greater-than (>) instead of greater-than-or-equal (>=). When size equals sizeof(copy) (32768), the comparison evaluates to false and size is not clamped to sizeof(copy)-1. The fix replaces the conditional with an unconditional size = min(sizeof(copy) - 1, size), ensuring size is always at most 32767.

tainted_value_origin.code: extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size)
tainted_value_origin.description: The size parameter from the libFuzzer entry point carries the attacker-controlled input length. When size equals exactly 32768, it triggers the off-by-one in the guard.

coarse_trace.summary: Receives attacker-controlled data and size from the fuzzer. Applies a size-clamping guard with an off-by-one error (> instead of >=), copies data into a global static buffer via memcpy, then NUL-terminates at copy[size]. When size equals sizeof(copy) (32768), the guard fails to clamp, and the NUL-termination writes 1 byte past the buffer end.

fine_trace.note: Size-clamping guard: size=32768 from the PoC, sizeof(copy)=32768. The strict greater-than comparison (32768 > 32768) evaluates to false, so the clamping body (size = sizeof(copy) - 1) is not executed and size remains 32768. The comparison should use >= to catch the boundary case where size equals sizeof(copy).

Copies 32768 bytes of attacker-controlled data into the 32768-byte global static array copy, completely filling it. The unclamped size=32768 is carried forward to the next statement for NUL-termination indexing.

ASAN reports global-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 at 0x0000011aa460 (0 bytes to the right of global variable copy defined at template_fuzzer.cc:57, size 32768).

parser_admitted.description: Attacker input of exactly 32768 bytes reaches the size-clamping guard. The guard (size > sizeof(copy)) evaluates to false because 32768 > 32768 is false, so execution falls through to memcpy and NUL-termination without clamping size.

format.contract: Exactly 32768 bytes of arbitrary content. The input length must equal sizeof(copy) (32768) so that the strict greater-than guard (size > sizeof(copy)) evaluates to false and size is not clamped, causing copy[32768] = '\0' to write 1 byte past the end of the buffer.
